expr: (list (condition-case e (compare-strings 1 0 1 "abc" 0 3) (error (cons (car e) (cdr e)))) (condition-case e (compare-strings "abc" 2 1 "abc" 0 3) (error (cons (car e) (cdr e)))) (condition-case e (compare-strings "abc" 0 3 (quote abc) 0 3) (error (cons (car e) (cdr e)))))
note: THE TWO ERRORS THAT ARE REAL, as values rather than as conditions so one case can hold both. Emacs answers ((wrong-type-argument stringp 1) (args-out-of-range "abc" 2 1) (wrong-type-argument stringp abc)). A non-string argument is `wrong-type-argument' with `(stringp N)' data -- and a SYMBOL is not coerced the way `assoc-string' coerces one, which is worth having in writing beside frontier-assoc-string-element-shapes since the two names sit one line apart in s.el. A START greater than its own END is `args-out-of-range' carrying (STRING START END), the one bounds shape frontier-compare-strings-bounds-clip-and-error does not cover, and the ordering is checked against the CLIPPED end. kg answers `void-function' at this pin. THIS CASE FLIPPED in the frontier demand phase: both errors are kg's now, including the START-past-END one being a RANGE failure rather than a type one.
